readings: Join each examination record to its patient's sex, keeping blank and missing sexes as their own groups. For each sex, count the number of examination records (rows in Examination), and give that count as a share of the overall total number of examination records. Then, for the sexes whose examination-record count is above the average count per sex group, return one row with their combined examination-record count, their average share, and the average amount by which their counts exceed the per-sex average count.

Join each examination record to its patient's sex, keeping blank and missing sexes as their own groups. For each sex, count the number of distinct patients who have at least one examination, and give that count as a share of the overall total number of distinct examined patients. Then, for the sexes whose distinct-patient count is above the average distinct-patient count per sex group, return one row with their combined distinct-patient count, their average share, and the average amount by which their counts exceed the per-sex average count.
queries:
WITH g AS (
    SELECT p.SEX AS sex, COUNT(*) AS cnt
    FROM Examination e
    LEFT JOIN Patient p ON e.ID = p.ID
    GROUP BY p.SEX
),
t AS (
    SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total, AVG(cnt) AS avg_cnt
    FROM g
)
SELECT SUM(g.cnt) AS combined_count,
       AVG(g.cnt * 1.0 / t.total) AS avg_share,
       AVG(g.cnt - t.avg_cnt) AS avg_excess
FROM g, t
WHERE g.cnt > t.avg_cnt;
WITH s AS (
    SELECT P.SEX AS sex, COUNT(DISTINCT E.ID) AS cnt
    FROM Examination E
    JOIN Patient P ON E.ID = P.ID
    GROUP BY P.SEX
),
t AS (
    SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT E.ID) AS total
    FROM Examination E
    JOIN Patient P ON E.ID = P.ID
),
a AS (
    SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_cnt FROM s
)
SELECT SUM(s.cnt) AS combined_distinct_patients,
       AVG(s.cnt * 1.0 / t.total) AS average_share,
       AVG(s.cnt - a.avg_cnt) AS average_excess
FROM s, t, a
WHERE s.cnt > a.avg_cnt;
